# Co-residency Test for GH200 (sm_90a)

## Why time-range overlap is not evidence of co-residency

Two kernels can have overlapping wall-clock intervals without ever running on
the same SM at the same instant.  The GPU scheduler may place kernel A on SMs
0-31 and kernel B on SMs 32-63; their `%globaltimer` ranges overlap, but no SM
ever hosts CTAs from both kernels simultaneously.  Conversely, the scheduler
might serialize them on the same SMs with no overlap at all.  Only by recording
the SM id (`%smid`) together with per-CTA start/stop timestamps can we detect
true co-residency: two CTAs are co-resident on SM *s* iff their time intervals
on *s* intersect.
